title: fix(webchat): keep saved replies visible during history refresh
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a saved background reply can remain missing, or disappear after appearing, when its WebChat transcript update races an older history request.

## User Impact

User impact: completed results remain visible without asking the agent to repeat them or manually reloading the conversation. No configuration, storage schema, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A transcript commit must invalidate a history read that began before it. Previously, idle panes could reuse the stale read without fetching the new result, while an active pane could admit the reply and then lose it when that stale snapshot advanced its transcript leaf.

The event handler now retires the older read before run settlement and uses the existing history loader's single queued refresh. Identity-only transcript invalidations use the same refresh contract. Session/connection fencing, branch replacement, message identity, and ordinary final delivery remain unchanged; there is no new retry loop or cache.

Contributor credit: Vito reported the missing final result and requested this repair.

## Worked on by

- @VACInc

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @VACInc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/09225428-6e0e-4e76-923a-ad7dfc41ab0a)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/1595be28-33d9-4e11-8347-76e7d1f93a56)

## Evidence

- All four mounted-pane regression cases fail on the original production code with an empty conversation result, then pass with the repair: late background reply, identity-only invalidation, active reply followed by an older leaf snapshot, and a reply whose event observes run settlement. The active cases first verify that the live report was actually admitted before the stale read resolves. Each case verifies one fresh read and one reply after reload.
- **151 focused and sibling tests passed across seven files**, including ordinary final/abort handling, in-flight history, cursor replay, retired-session fencing, successor-session isolation, and shared pane events.
- UI production typechecking, all UI test-type shards, changed-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh AutoReview is scoped-clean through P2. An independent source review identified both history races before the final repair.
- Actual Chromium with the real Control UI and synthetic Gateway events reproduced **zero visible replies / one history read before**, and **one visible reply / two history reads after**. Sanitized before/after captures are shown below.

### CI follow-up

The first ready-PR CI run failed `checks-ui (1/3)` at `chat-state.test.ts:2637`: an older peer-message test still expected the superseded history request to be the only read. The same case failed deterministically in the CI UI configuration with three workers. This was a stale test expectation, not a transient runner failure.

The follow-up changes tests only: separate stale/fresh snapshots, three peer commits sharing exactly one successor read (two total RPCs), unchanged one-frame/canonical-message assertions, and an awaited history owner instead of polling. **302 selected tests passed across eight files** in the CI UI configuration with three workers. The corrected `chat-state.test.ts` also passed all 151 cases with one worker (**3.63 seconds wall**); UI test types, lint, formatting, and fresh AutoReview through P2 passed. Exact-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper readiness remain required.

### Before and after

**Before** — the saved result is absent after the older history read settles.

![Before: saved result missing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3eedac46-4b68-4c6c-958a-bcbd959be9e1)

**After** — one fresh read restores the saved result once.

![After: saved result visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/124d1f98-7d5f-45ab-914c-892a3e7ef4f8)

The original browser's event timing was not recorded. This proves reproducible UI loss mechanisms for a saved reply, not the exact historical WebSocket sequence. Browser proof uses controlled Gateway responses, not live provider execution.

### Test cost

`pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-reply-invalidation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **3.26 seconds wall**; the four cases total about **0.47 seconds**. The seven-file sibling run took **7.82 seconds wall**. No sleeps or polling were added to the tests. Full CI and the refreshed ClawSweeper review are required on the follow-up head.
